To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ca2+-dependent binding of centrin to transducin in photoreceptor cells is the first demonstration of the interaction of a G-protein with a Ca2+-binding regulatory protein.

the Ca2+-activated Ca2+-binding centrin 1 protein forms a stable complex with the G-protein subunits βγ in the connecting cilium of rod photoreceptor cells and that this assembly is regulated by the intracellular Ca2+ concentration.

centrin 1, a Ca(2+)-binding protein of the photoreceptor connecting cilium, assembles with the heterotrimeric visual G protein transducin through a Ca(2+) -dependent mechanism that involves the βγ-subunit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of light adaptation in the retina.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the translocation of signaling proteins in photoreceptor cells.
the assembly of a heterotrimer of the visual G protein with a Ca2+-binding regulatory protein in the photoreceptor cilium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the centrin-G protein complex is formed by the interaction of centrin 1 with the βγ complex of the G protein.
the centrin 1 protein is an important component of the cilium and that centrin 1 is involved in the regulation of the light-induced exchange of G proteins between the outer and the inner segment.
centrin is an integral part of the transduction cascade and that the centrin-G-proteins complex may serve as a molecular motor in the cilium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
centrin 1, a Ca2+-binding EF-hand protein, binds to the βγ-complexe of the heterotrimeric transducin, and that this interaction is regulated by Ca2+.
we found that transducin is a target for Ca2+-dependent centrin binding in photoreceptor cilia and that this binding is mediated by the transducin βγ-complex.
the centrin 1-G protein complex may be involved in the regulation of the G-protein cycle in photoreceptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
centrin 1 and transducin colo-calize in a specific domain in the cilium and that centrin 2 and transducin 1 interact.
Ca2+-binding proteins can be involved in the assembly of G-protein complexes and that the G protein βγ-subunit is a key player in this process.
centrin is a Ca2+-activated G protein-binding protein.
